_note: ALL VALUES ARE NOMINAL ASSUMPTIONS — calibrate with real suit data before trusting them. Exception: the radiation block is a published measurement.
_budget_note: Metabolic energy for one 8 h EVA at 1200 BTU/h (351.7 W): the Apollo PLSS design average and NASA's expected sizing rate for future EVAs in planetary gravity (Waligora et al., NASA TN D-7883; NASA ICES 2026, NTRS 20260005410). The ISS EMU basis (1000 BTU/h) would give 8.44 MJ, and then the default route fails. The EVA clock slider (0 to 8 h) walks the crew along the route at walk_speed_ms, then they stay at the destination doing station work: Pandolf walking energy is charged for the distance covered and every other second (station work, rest) at 351.7 W (budget / duration), so the walk-back envelope shrinks as the clock runs. The turnaround time is when the energy left, minus the walk-back with margin, runs out. return_margin 0.2 follows Apollo walkback practice (1440 = 1.2 x 1200 BTU/h).
